buyingCommitteeStructure.typical: 3–5 people involved in commercial furniture decisions above $30,000

roles.visionary: CEO/MD — sets vision, approves final spend
roles.gatekeeper: CFO — controls budget, demands value justification
roles.champion: Office Manager/EA — day-to-day champion, does the research, advocates internally
roles.influencer: IT Manager, Facilities Manager — input on technical and logistics requirements
roles.advisor: External interior designer or architect — may specify products; get specified by them

buyingCommitteeStructure.strategyImplication: Identify the champion early and invest in them. They will close the deal internally if equipped correctly.

threeQuoteRule.description: Most Australian corporates require 3 quotes for purchases above $30,000
threeQuoteRule.TCDStrategy: Be first on the table. The first quote sets the reference price. All subsequent quotes are evaluated against yours.
threeQuoteRule.priceAnchoringAdvantage: Being first gives structural pricing leverage. Being last means you're competing against an established benchmark.
threeQuoteRule.winningFirstQuote: Offer the layout plan first. This creates engagement, demonstrates expertise, and gets TCD into the process before competitors are contacted.

ranked.action: Call within 48 hours. They are 6–8 weeks from furniture decisions.
Reach out with free layout plan offer referencing their team size.
Position office refresh as essential to brand consistency.
Coordinate delivery with building access windows.
Reach out within 1 week. New funding often triggers office expansion.
Lead with sit-stand desk upgrade programme and ergonomic seating.

budgetCyclePatterns.corporate_EOFY: June 30 — major approval period. Pitch April–May for EOFY budget inclusion.
budgetCyclePatterns.corporate_Q4: October–December — post-EOFY budget approval. Highest volume commercial furniture buying period.
budgetCyclePatterns.corporate_Q1: February–March — new financial year planning. Second highest buying period.
budgetCyclePatterns.government: June EOFY — tender for budget inclusion April–May.
budgetCyclePatterns.implication: Run campaigns and prospecting August–October and January–February to catch budget-holding decision-makers.

needMoreTime.realMeaning: The internal champion hasn't gotten sign-off from the CFO or CEO yet.
needMoreTime.response: Ask who else needs to be involved and offer to present directly to them. Provide an internal presentation deck for the champion.

tooExpensive.realMeaning: The buyer hasn't justified the value internally and needs language to do so.
tooExpensive.response: Give them the TCO argument: 6-year warranty vs replacing cheap furniture at year 2–3. Calculate the cost difference in writing.

lookingAtOptions.realMeaning: They want reassurance they're not missing a better option.
lookingAtOptions.response: Send a comparison framework positioning TCD's quality, warranty, and service. Never disparage competitors by name.

budgetTight.realMeaning: Either genuine budget constraint or they haven't internalised the value case.
budgetTight.response: Present finance option first. Then offer the Foundation tier. Only discount if you've made the full value case first.
